title: Prize shelves and special displays
summary: Not every shelf in TCG Card Shop Simulator exists just to sell: the game defines shelves for particular purposes, including a shelf that exists for tournament prizes.
body: Shelves are typed in the game, so a display can be built for a specific job rather than being one generic rack.
A prize shelf shows that some goods are handled as awards rather than ordinary stock, which is a different purpose from selling.

A prize shelf is furnished like a shelf and pointed at like a stall. It carries its own compartments and a screen of its own, a place for a customer to stand and a separate list of places for winners, which is why a display for prizes is set up rather than just placed.

It is also told how to behave around a controller. The shelf keeps a reversed quick-select sequence and a listener for electronic cards, and it is marked with an object type along with whether it cuts the navmesh or counts as a generic object.
Whatever the purpose, shelf contents are tracked the same way, so keeping the display full is still a task you have to do.
What this entry does not tell you: what a tournament pays, how often one runs or what belongs on a prize shelf. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: A shelf dedicated to tournament prizes exists.
Shelves are typed rather than being one generic rack.
Shelf contents are tracked by a manager regardless of the shelf's purpose.
The prize shelf has its own compartments and a screen mesh, with a stand location for customers and a separate list of stand locations for winners.
